A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the OPE allows us to obtain the decay/annihilation rates at any finite temperature in terms of the zero-tempera-ture rate and the thermal mass, which is the leading thermal correction.

, in thermal field theory, a decay or annihilation process is dominated by the zero-temperature matrix elements, and thermal effects can be treated perturbatively in a multiplicative way, with the leading thermal correction being of order T4/m4.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the leading thermal corrections to the decay width and annihilation rate are given by the thermal expectation values of the same local operators that appear in the zero-temperature field theoretical calculation.

the thermal modification of the decay and annhilation rate of a heavy particle in the medium is given by the same factor as that of the decay rate in the vacuum, and is independent of whether the decay or annihilation is two-body or multi-body, and whether the final state particles are massive or massless.
the leading thermal corrections to decay and annihilation rates are the same as the leading quantum corrections in the zero-temperature limit.
